findings.title: Highest can't select a non-positive priority
findings.detail: bestPriority starts at 0, so a task whose priority is 0 or negative never replaces it; when every priority is non-positive, Highest returns "".
findings.risk_rationale: A queue of only non-positive priorities silently returns no winner.

findings.title: priority.go could use strings.Builder too
findings.detail: Same style point as the dismissed one: building output without strings.Builder.
findings.risk_rationale: A style point, not a measured cost at expected queue sizes.

summary: Highest has a zero floor bug. A style note also cites the dismissed labels.go point, but against the wrong file.
